uncited: This family defines methods for converting continuous geometric primitives (points, lines, planes, triangles) into discrete volumetric representations (voxel grids) suitable for volume rendering.
It solves the problem of accurately representing sharp geometric boundaries within a scalar field without the aliasing artifacts inherent in binary voxelization.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md) by focusing on analytic slab definitions, optimal scanline criteria, and priority-based clipping rather than GPU rasterization pipelines or geometry shaders.
The method originates from the need to hybridize ray tracing and volume rendering.

detail: supported

To avoid these artifacts, Kaufman et al. proposed bandlimiting objects to the Nyquist frequency and using volume rendering's partial opacity to handle the resulting voxel representation [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that to avoid aliasing artifacts common in binary voxel representations, the object must be bandlimited to the Nyquist frequency and sampled to limit quantization losses. It further explains that volume rendering's ability to represent partial opacity makes it suitable for handling the resulting voxel representation. The attribution to Kaufman et al. is consistent with the citations provided in the text ([Kaufman 1986], [Kaufman 1987a]).
